news.title: US World Cup host cities say FIFA owes them millions: Report
news.lede: US cities that hosted the 2026 World Cup contend that FIFA owes them US$1 million (S$1.3 million) in “legacy” funds to build mini-pitches and support “social projects” in their cities. NEW YORK – US cities that hosted the 2026 World Cup contend FIFA owes them millions of dollars promised to them, The Athletic reported on Aug 4. Four executives from World Cup cities, speaking anonymously, told the outlet that FIFA management told them they would each receive US$1 million (S$1.3 million) in “legacy” funds to build mini-pitches and support “social projects” in their cities. That was the same amount of money that cities hosting the Club World Cup in 2025 were promised by Gianni Infantino, FIFA president, in a public announcement.

news.title: Wenger and Infantino’s No 2 Grafström criticise ‘sad and reproachable’ World Cup plan
news.lede: Senior Fifa duo pile pressure on under-fire president. Wenger reveals he knew nothing about investment plan. Gianni Infantino’s authority was dealt a further blow after his No 2, the Fifa secretary general, Mattias Grafström, called the failed World Cup private investment plan a “sad and reproachable series of events”. In further evidence that senior Fifa personnel continue to distance themselves from Infantino and his botched scheme, Arsène Wenger issued a statement on Tuesday morning saying the project’s withdrawal was “absolutely necessary and beyond question”.

news.title: Top Fifa executive Wenger condemns move to reform World Cup business plan
news.lede: Former Arsenal coach Arsène Wenger on Tuesday became the latest top executive at world football's governing body Fifa to distance himself from the failed plan of Fifa boss Gianni Infantino to sell stakes in future World Cup profits to private investors. Infantino hired Wenger in 2019 as Fifa's head of global football development and over the past seven years, the Frenchman has masterminded Fifa's quest to make sure talented players around the world are spotted and developed. But the 76-year-old, who transformed the culture and playing style of top flight football in England in the late 1990s and early 2000s, criticised the proposals to reform the commercial side of Fifa competitions without explicitly naming Infantino. “I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports,” said Wenger.

news.title: Arsene Wenger breaks silence on FIFA World Cup sale plan as Gianni Infantino pressure mounts
news.lede: Arsene Wenger has made it clear he played no part in Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions. During the World Cup, Wenger, who is FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development , was regularly seen alongside Infantino. Not long after Infantino's plan to introduce a commercial subsidiary of FIFA called 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' to allow outside investors to purchase stocks in competitions affiliated with the governing body of world football, Wenger received some criticism for, what was seen by some, as silence while the plans were revealed by the media. The widely-detested idea has since been put to rest after it received the thumbs down from UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Federation.

news.title: World Cup football drives “solid" financial results for ITV
news.lede: UK broadcaster ITV has reported a “solid” performance in its first half of 2026 financial results, with the football World Cup driving a 3% growth in advertising despite “macro-economic headwinds”. Overall, the company’s total group revenue rose 2% to £1.89bn from £1.85bn the previous year. Pretax profit increased 16% to £78m from £67m. According to ITV, the Men’s Football World Cup drove the revenue growth.

news.title: Oliver Baumann says Julian Nagelsmann apologized after World Cup benching
news.lede: Germany goalkeeper Oliver Baumann has opened up about one of the toughest moments of his career after Julian Nagelsmann opted to restore Manuel Neuer as the starting goalkeeper for the World Cup. Baumann had established himself as Germany’s No. 1 leading up to the tournament, but Nagelsmann, leaning on input from some key players, ultimately turned back to Neuer for football’s biggest stage. While the decision was undoubtedly disappointing for Baumann, the goalkeeper sayid that the ex-Germany coach, who was recently replaced by Jürgen Klopp, reached out afterward to discuss everything openly. “He [Nagelsmann] was sorry about how everything turned out in the end.

news.title: Tottenham offered transfer deal for ex-Arsenal ace embroiled in World Cup controversy
news.lede: Tottenham have reportedly been offered the chance to sign former Arsenal youngster Folarin Balogun. The 25-year-old has been the subject of discussions between the Lilywhites and intermediaries, according to reports. Balogun's representatives are claimed to have contacted Spurs directly with a proposal for the Monaco star, who came through Arsenal's academy. The striker is said to be available for a 'competitive fee.

news.title: FIFA denies Infantino sought Trump backing after failed World Cup selloff
news.lede: Who is tipped to replace Gianni Infantino after the World Cup investment plan crisis? UEFA, who were the strongest opponents of FIFA’s plan, slam the Gianni Infantino-led governing body despite standdown. Al Jazeera looks at the growing global opposition to FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s private investment plan. What do the charges brought against Argentina’s FA, their players and their fans mean, and what action could FIFA take?
